data.title: Dissecting forceps
data.summary: Forceps & clamps · Non-locking V-shaped spring forceps used to hold tissue during dissection, suturing and dressing.
data.body:
![Dissecting forceps](instruments/dissecting-forceps.jpg)

_Also called: Thumb forceps, Tissue forceps, Pick-ups, Plain / toothed forceps_

Non-locking V-shaped spring forceps used to hold tissue during dissection, suturing and dressing.

## Parts
- Two blades/arms fused at one end and free at the other
- Tips plain (serrated) or toothed
- No ratchet or lock

## Types / variants
- Plain (non-toothed) - transverse serrations, less traumatic; for nerves, biopsy tissue and delicate structures
- Toothed - usually 2 teeth on one jaw interlocking with 1 on the other (1x2); firmer grip, more traumatic; for dermis and cyst walls

## Uses / indications
- Holding tissue during dissection, suturing and dressing
- Plain: delicate structures, biopsy specimens
- Toothed: skin/dermis, cyst wall

## How to hold
Hold like a pen with the first three fingers (between thumb and middle finger, index finger steadying); grasp dermis rather than epidermis to avoid crushing the wound edge.

## Sterilisation & care
Autoclave, hot air oven, 2% glutaraldehyde or boiling

## Viva points & tips
- Do not crush the epidermis - pick up dermis
- Plain = less traumatic; toothed = better grip but more traumatic
